chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Abu Ali al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar from Safwan from Ibn Muskhan, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the meat of donkeys, so he said: 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) forbade eating it on the day of Khaybar.' I asked him about eating horses and mules, so he said: 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) forbade them, so do not eat them unless you are compelled to do so.'
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on eating donkey, horse, and mule meat according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the distinction between the absolute prohibition (*haram*) of domestic donkey meat, established by the Prophet at Khaybar, and the conditional prohibition (*makruh* or permissible under necessity) of horses and mules. It reflects the Shia juristic principle that while these animals are not typically slaughtered for food, their meat becomes lawful in cases of dire need (*darura*), aligning with the broader Islamic legal framework of necessity overriding prohibition.
